Wichita, mean annual PET 830 mm Thornthwaite, 1,220 mm Hargreaves 1,490 mm Penman. Thornthwaite’s method uses mean temperature , gives almost PET cold months. Penman’s method physically based accurate data available; Hargreaves’ method common alternative temperature available. Penman series also gaps wind sunshine data missing. choice PET method affects SPEI, worth reporting. use Hargreaves PET, needs missing-data handling:
code: lat <- 37.6475  pet_tho <- thornthwaite(wichita[, "TMED"], lat) #> Checking for missing values (`NA`): all the data must be complete. Input type is tsvector. Time series spanning Jan 1980 to Oct 2011. pet_har <- hargreaves(wichita[, "TMIN"], wichita[, "TMAX"], lat = lat) #> Calculating reference evapotranspiration using the Hargreaves method. Using latitude (`lat`) to estimate extraterrestrial radiation. Checking for missing values (`NA`): all the data must be complete. Input type is tsvector. Time series spanning Jan 1980 to Oct 2011. pet_pen <- penman(wichita[, "TMIN"], wichita[, "TMAX"], wichita[, "AWND"],   tsun = wichita[, "TSUN"], lat = lat, z = 402.6, na.rm = TRUE ) #> Using user-provided wind speed at 2 m height (`U2`) data. Using latitude (`lat`) to estimate extraterrestrial radiation. Using bright sunshine duration data (`tsun`) to estimate incoming solar radiation. Using minimum temperature (`Tmin`) to estimate dewpoint temperature and actual vapour pressure (Tdew = Tmin - aT, with `aT` = 0). Assuming constant atmospheric surface pressure corresponding to elevation `z`. Computing for a short crop. Missing values (`NA`) will not be considered in the calculation. Input type is tsvector. Time series spanning Jan 1980 to Oct 2011. Calculation method is ICID. pet <- cbind(Thornthwaite = pet_tho, Hargreaves = pet_har, Penman = pet_pen) plot(window(pet, start = c(2000, 1), end = c(2004, 12)),   plot.type = "single", col = 1:3, ylab = "PET (mm)" ) legend("topleft", colnames(pet), col = 1:3, lty = 1, bty = "n") bal <- wichita[, "PRCP"] - pet_har
